questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact. This prevents the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see clearly to the sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see clearly to the sides.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet lets you see clearly to the sides for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels showing the manufacturer's name, instructions, and safety standards.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, make sure you can see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirror to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. A properly adjusted mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but what matters most is seeing the road behind and to the side.

questions.question: Motorcycle signals are:

options.text: Even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
Only needed when another vehicle is right next to you.
Less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. Because of this, using signals properly is even more important for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required equipment for a motorcycle:

options.text: A blue reflector on the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blue reflector on the rear.
questions.explanation: In Utah, motorcycles must have: one headlamp; one taillamp; a white light for the rear license plate; one red reflector on the rear; a stop lamp; brakes; a horn or warning device; a muffler; a mirror; tires with at least 2/32 inch tread depth; footrests for passengers; handlebars; and turn signals if made after 1973. A blue rear reflector is not required.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects are:

options.text: More dangerous than using either alone.
Less dangerous than using either alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than using either alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can make it unsafe to ride. When combined with alcohol, some medications become even more dangerous.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries are reduced by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Skip a jacket if it's warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of proper material when riding, even in warm weather. A jacket helps prevent dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist:
questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Protective clothing for riders includes jackets and sturdy pants that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves. A stocking cap is not protective motorcycle clothing.

questions.question: Before riding, check that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes create friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Check each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and holds the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Can low-speed crashes be dangerous?

options.text: No, they happen often so they are not a concern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can be fatal.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can cause death.

questions.question: When should you increase the space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When stopping will be harder than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver ahead from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than usual.
questions.explanation: Increase your space cushion when your motorcycle needs longer to stop. This includes slippery pavement, poor visibility, or heavy traffic where drivers may cut in front of you.

questions.question: What material are motorcycle riding gloves usually made of?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: What is one feature of an approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
It does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A helmet approved by the U.S. Department of Transportation will not limit your vision. You will be able to see as far as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: What should you do with shoelaces when riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tuck them in.
questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoelaces securely so they do not catch on your motorcycle.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take and how often should you do it?

options.text: A few minutes, once a month.
A few minutes, before every ride.
Over an hour, done by a mechanic.
Over an hour, only when carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes, before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: How should you ride when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Your motorcycle will accelerate, turn, and stop more slowly. Ride slower, start slowing sooner, leave more space between vehicles, and wait for bigger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: What type of shoe soles should motorcycle riders wear?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hard, durable, and slip-resistant.
questions.explanation: Wear riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy. Choose footwear with soles made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: How noticeable is a motorcycle brake light compared to a car's brake light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers notice you.

questions.question: The faster you drink, the more:

options.text: Alcohol builds up in your body.
Your body fights off the alcohol's effects.
You can avoid being stopped by police.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the more alcohol builds up in your body. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get away from them.
Move onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass you.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely if you can so they can get in front of you. Speeding up only makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend in and not be noticed by other drivers.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Drive very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: Make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake lights, and position yourself correctly in your lane. Keep safe distance from other vehicles and look ahead 12 seconds to spot hazards.

questions.question: What best protects your head and neck in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to prevent head and neck injuries if you crash.

questions.question: When your turn is obvious, you:

options.text: Don't need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need a turn signal at stop lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when you turn or change lanes. Other vehicles may be nearby even if you can't see them. Signals are required every time, no exceptions.
